title: Monthly budget variance summary
source: written for ticket 35 from Johnny's edge case in AI Fluency Levels scoring rules v1 (he gave a description, not a chat): "A great plain chat with no agent". Every name and figure is invented.

turns.user: Every month I turn our six department budget reports into one variance summary for the CFO. Output one table: department, budget, actual, variance %, one-line reason. Use only what the reports say. If a reason isn't stated, write 'not stated' and I'll chase it. Don't round.
turns.assistant: Understood. Send the reports and I'll build the table with those rules.
Here is the table for all six departments. Marketing: budget 50,000, actual 52,100, variance 3.8%, reason not stated. Sales: budget 80,000, actual 86,000, variance 7.5%, reason seasonal demand.

turns.user: Two checks. Marketing's variance is 4.2%, not 3.8%: 52,100 against 50,000. And 'seasonal demand' for Sales isn't in their report. Mark it not stated, and list every reason you inferred rather than read.
turns.assistant: Corrected: Marketing 4.2%, Sales reason not stated. I inferred two reasons: Sales and Facilities. Facilities is now not stated too.

turns.user: Good. Before April, list what in this format would break if a department changes its cost codes, and what you would check first.
turns.assistant: Three things would break: the budget line match, the year-to-date totals and the department mapping. I would check the mapping first.

turns.user: Use the mapping check and the totals check from that list on every run. Same rules on April: [six reports pasted]
turns.assistant: Checks passed on five departments. Legal's total doesn't match its report by 300, so I have left it out and flagged it. Here is the table.

turns.user: Keep these rules as the template I paste in each month. I decide which variances go to the CFO, so stop at the table.
turns.assistant: Here is the template with the rules and the two checks.
